statusText:
Nothing has traded. The CME weekend halt still governs the published state: NQ futures have not quoted since Friday 14 August and Globex does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, about nine and a half hours from this run. Tail stays low at 14%, the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the last observed path was benign.

The marginal news this hour runs mildly the other way from last hour's escalation, which is why Stress eases from 80% to 78% rather than climbing again. A Hamas delegation met Egypt's intelligence chief Hassan Rashad to discuss implementing a 15-point postwar plan that Netanyahu had previously rejected, and talks with US officials and the Board of Peace's Nickolay Mladenov are being arranged around Jared Kushner's regional visit. No new kinetic escalation has been reported since Saturday's south-Lebanon strikes and the Gaza tank incident.

Those Saturday events remain the reason Stress sits in the high band at all. Israeli strikes on south Lebanon killed 11 people, the deadliest day since the June ceasefire, and the IDF has identified a second senior Hezbollah commander killed in them; Defence Minister Katz has vowed to settle scores. An IDF tank was hit by an explosive device in Gaza in what the military called a grave truce violation. That is a real, unresolved escalation sitting on a closed tape with a diplomatic channel now visibly opening against it - a conflicting signal set, which the contract says should raise Stress rather than Tail.

One correction to the record carried from earlier runs: VIX closed Friday at 14.25, down 2.60%, against a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30. That is near the bottom of the range but is not the low of 2026. Low implied volatility is thin cushion into an unpriced restart - a Stress statement, not a Tail one.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 14% maps to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always.

The roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window is anchored to it at 21:55-00:00 UTC, 23:55-02:00 Berlin. That is deliberately narrower than a whole-session shutdown: the risk is concentrated in the gap itself and the first two hours of thin Asian-transition liquidity, where a full weekend of Lebanon, Gaza and Hormuz headlines meets a market that closed with implied volatility near the bottom of its 52-week range. Forecast Tail drifts 14% to 19% through the remaining halt, steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting - orange, block new base entries - before easing through the watch band and returning to green at 05:00 UTC Monday.

This is general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and it is not a recommendation to place any trade.
headline: CME weekend halt holds with about nine and a half hours to the Globex restart: Friday's NQ close of 30,141.75 was benign and VIX finished at 14.25, and with a Hamas-Egypt diplomatic channel opening against Saturday's south-Lebanon escalation Stress eases to 78% - Tail stays low at 14%, EA_ON and green, Confidence 76%
body:
Observed reference levels, all from Friday 14 August's close because nothing has traded since. NQU26 settled at 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, opening at 30,210.75 against a 30,188.50 previous close and holding a 254-point range of 30,028.50 to 30,283.00. It finished mid-range, roughly 2.7% below the 52-week high of 30,975.50 and far above the 22,961.50 low. There is no persistent directional efficiency in that, no shallow-pullback extension, no repeated failed retracement and no close near an extreme - the four things the contract requires before Tail belongs above 25%.

Cash indices agreed, re-verified from primary quote pages this hour. The Nasdaq Composite closed 26,729.16, down 73.86 or 0.28%, inside a 26,661.95 to 26,862.17 day range and against a 52-week range of 20,690.25 to 27,190.21 - about 1.7% below its high. The S&P 500 closed 7,785 and the Dow 53,732, both down around 0.2%, while the Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 3,068, a fresh record. On the week the S&P added 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.1% while the Dow fell 0.6%. VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60%, day range 14.18 to 14.72, 52-week range 13.38 to 35.30.

Breadth is the single most useful equity observation available. A small-cap record set on a day the Nasdaq fell is broadening, not the narrow mega-cap leadership that typically precedes a one-way index break. Semiconductors were dispersed rather than aligned - Broadcom fell 5.9% and Intel 2% with Nvidia slightly lower, while AMD gained 6.5%, Micron 2.3% and SanDisk 7.4% - and dispersion inside the complex is the opposite of the alignment that would manufacture index-level one-way structure.

Rates and commodities. The 2-year yield finished at 4.17%, up 3.1bp on the day but down 3.2bp on the week; the 10-year at 4.695%, up 5.6bp on the day and 3.8bp on the week - a modest bear-steepening, not a cross-asset stress impulse. WTI is $82.40, up $1.15 or 1.42% on Friday and roughly 5% on the week and 33% year on year; Brent $88.52, up $1.45 or 1.67% and 34% year on year. That is the standing price of a closed Hormuz, with the IEA warning of deeper global deficits. Gold added $16.90 to $4,437.30.

The Hormuz file has not moved today. The strait has been effectively shut since late February, Iran and Oman describe their vessel-movement talks as close to done, but Tehran's foreign ministry maintains that no reopening is possible while the US naval blockade continues, and Iran additionally demands sanctions relief and reparations. The Axios-reported IRGC backchannel endorsement of Tehran's negotiators remains the most constructive datum on the file; it removes an obstacle, it does not open the strait.

Friday's macro was genuinely soft and still deserves to be carried forward. July retail sales fell 0.6%, the worst print since May 2025, and preliminary consumer sentiment came in at 51.0 against 54.5 expected. Equities took this benignly because it reduced perceived odds of a September Fed hike, but a weakening consumer is a real seed for a growth scare and is part of why Stress sits high while Tail does not.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour. The seven-day US list is front-loaded with housing and survey data, with FOMC Minutes on Wednesday 19 August at 18:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed index on Thursday, and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday 21 August as the high-impact anchors. Industrial production and capacity utilisation are omitted because sources disagree materially on the release time. July existing-home sales are not in the window - that report was released on 11 August, showing a 1.7% decline to a 4.06 million annual rate. Jackson Hole falls on 27-29 August, outside this window, with Kevin Warsh due to give his first keynote as Fed chair on 28 August; the larger catalyst sits just beyond the seven-day horizon.

Evidence quality. Confidence 76%. Index and futures levels, day and 52-week ranges, VIX, oil, breadth, sector detail, weekend geopolitics and the seven-day calendar were read directly from primary pages this hour and are mutually consistent; one earlier VIX characterisation was corrected against the primary quote. Two fetches were refused this run - CNBC's week-ahead article and its VIX quote page returned 403, MarketWatch's calendar was unreachable - and each was replaced from an alternative primary source, so no input was lost. The one irreducible gap is that no live price path exists at all. During a scheduled venue halt that absence is a certain, known fact rather than an unreliable reading, which is why it caps Confidence at the low end of the high band rather than pushing it down.

lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 12:00 UTC Saturday to 11:00 UTC Sunday and sit entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours and the outcome was identical each time: EA_ON, green, dominantMode mixed. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 14%. Stress carried all the movement, running 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then dipping to 70 and climbing 71, 71, 78, 79, 78 and 80. Confidence rose almost monotonically from 61% to 75%.

Two features of that track matter for reading the current hour. First, most of the Stress climb from 53 to 80 happened across a market that never quoted once. Part of it is genuine - Saturday's south-Lebanon strikes are new information - but part is a re-reading of a static evidence set as the reopen approaches, and that component should not be extrapolated mechanically. This hour is the test: with no new escalation and a visible diplomatic channel opening, Stress comes down two points to 78% rather than continuing up, which is what an honest reading of conflicting signals requires.

Second, the near-monotonic Confidence rise is genuine and continues to 76%. Successive hours added primary-source coverage of levels, volatility, rates, oil, breadth and the calendar even though the price path stayed unavailable, and this hour corrected an inherited VIX characterisation against the primary quote. Tail's 10-to-14 drift across the whole window is the smallest movement in the set, which is the correct behaviour when the input that drives Tail - observed price path - has been absent for every single slot.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 11:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart and the first thirteen hours of live quoting sit inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for the nine remaining halt slots, drifting 14% to 19%, then steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 24%, 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 05:00 UTC Monday, settling at 17% through the European morning. Forecast status is yellow at 21:00 UTC, orange at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 04:00 UTC Monday and green thereafter.

That orange is conditional risk about the reopen, not an assertion that a one-way path has been observed. The reasoning is mechanical: a full weekend of unpriced Lebanon, Gaza and Hormuz headlines has to clear into a single restart in thin liquidity, against a market whose implied volatility closed near the bottom of its 52-week range. If the gap is small and mean-reverting within the first hour, these forecast numbers will prove too high and the next assessments should say so plainly.

Stress rises from 78% to a peak of 86% at the restart, then decays to 74% by 11:00 UTC Monday as the weekend stack is absorbed. Confidence dips to 73% through the last hours of the halt as Friday's evidence ages, then rises sharply to 85-86% once live quoting restores the price path that is the single missing input. dominantMode is mixed throughout except for event/whipsaw across the four hours spanning the restart.

No high-impact US macro release falls inside this 24-hour window - the Empire State index at 12:30 UTC Monday sits just past it, and the FOMC Minutes, jobless claims and flash PMIs are Wednesday through Friday. The restart itself is therefore the only genuine checkpoint in the forecast, and Jackson Hole with Warsh's first keynote as chair on 27-29 August is the larger catalyst just past the horizon.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. CME is shut, no venue is quoting NQ or the NAS100 CFD, and no one-way price path can form. Tail 14% is a statement about a frozen tape, not about calm; Stress 78% carries the unpriced weekend stack of Lebanon strikes, a fraying Gaza truce and a closed Hormuz.

Still nine hours from the Globex restart. Expect no change in observable evidence during this hour - only headline flow can move the assessment, and the marginal news since the last run has been diplomatic rather than kinetic.

Tail edges to 15% purely because the reopen is one hour nearer; there is still nothing to observe. Stress ticks to 79% as the window in which weekend headlines can accumulate without being priced continues to run.
European Sunday afternoon. Evidence begins to age - Friday's closes are now more than 48 hours old - which is why Confidence starts drifting down while the price-path gap stays absolute.

Tail 16%, still low band, still EA_ON and green. Stress crosses to 80% as the last quiet stretch before the restart begins and the market has had a full weekend of Middle East headlines with no mechanism to price them.

Six hours to the restart. Any Sunday-evening statement out of Beirut, Jerusalem, Tehran or Washington now lands close enough to the reopen to influence the gap directly, so Stress keeps climbing while Tail stays in the low band.
